### [1] Agent Contracts: A Formal Framework for Resource-Bounded Autonomous AI Systems

- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/html/2601.08815v1
- **Type:** Academic paper (arXiv, January 2025)
- **Tier:** T1
- **Data extracted:** Formal contract tuple C = (I, O, S, R, T, Φ, Ψ) for agent
  resource governance. Conservation law: ∑(consumption) ≤ B(resource). Three
  allocation strategies: proportional, equal, negotiated. Code review experiment:
  90% token reduction with 525× lower variance vs uncontracted. Research pipeline:
  zero conservation violations across 50 trials. Crisis communication: 23% token
  reduction with equivalent quality. Documented $47,000 API bill from uncontrolled
  multi-agent system. Fundamental limitation: token consumption known only after
  LLM call completes, not during generation.
- **Accessed:** 2026-04-02

### [2] Token-Budget-Aware LLM Reasoning (TALE)

- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/html/2412.18547v1
- **Type:** Academic paper (arXiv, December 2024; ACL 2025 Findings)
- **Tier:** T1
- **Data extracted:** Framework for dynamic token budget allocation. Three
  estimators: zero-shot, regression, budget awareness internalization. Average
  68.64% output token reduction vs vanilla CoT. 59% expense reduction. Accuracy
  81.03% vs 83.75% vanilla CoT (< 3% decline). GSM8K-Zero: 98.72% accuracy with
  22.67 vs 252.96 tokens. Cross-model generalization across GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini,
  Yi-lightning. Token elasticity phenomenon: excessively small budgets
  paradoxically increase consumption.
- **Accessed:** 2026-04-02

### [3] ACON: Optimizing Context Compression for Long-horizon LLM Agents

- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.00615
- **Type:** Academic paper (arXiv, October 2025)
- **Tier:** T1
- **Data extracted:** Unified compression framework using natural language
  guidelines. 26-54% reduction in peak tokens across AppWorld, OfficeBench,
  Multi-objective QA. Distillation retains 95% accuracy. Enables 32% improvement
  (AppWorld), 20% (OfficeBench), 46% (Multi-objective QA) for smaller LMs.
  Gradient-free optimization works with API-accessible models.
- **Accessed:** 2026-04-02

### [4] Token Management in Multi-Tenant AI Inference Platforms

- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00356v1
- **Type:** Academic paper (arXiv, March 2025)
- **Tier:** T1
- **Data extracted:** Token pools as capacity abstraction: token throughput

### [6] Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval

- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/html/2510.05381v1
- **Type:** Academic paper (arXiv, October 2025)
- **Tier:** T1
- **Data extracted:** Performance degrades 13.9%-85% as input length increases
  even with perfect retrieval. Llama-3.1-8B: 24.2% accuracy drop on MMLU at 30K
  tokens despite perfect retrieval. Degradation persists when distraction tokens
  replaced with whitespace or masked during attention. Input length itself
  undermines reasoning independent of retrieval failures. Retrieve-then-solve
  improved GPT-4o on RULER by up to 4%.
- **Accessed:** 2026-04-02

### [13] Context Rot: Why LLMs Degrade as Context Grows

- **URL:** https://www.trychroma.com/research/context-rot
- **Type:** Research study (Chroma, 2025)
- **Tier:** T2
- **Data extracted:** 18 LLMs tested across Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Alibaba.
  Extended NIAH with semantic matching, LongMemEval, repeated words tasks. 8
  input lengths, 11 needle positions. Performance grows increasingly unreliable
  with length. Degradation faster with lower needle-question similarity. Shuffled
  haystacks improve performance vs logical flow. Degradation onset: 250-500 words
  (position accuracy), 2,500+ words (significant drops). Claude models most
  conservative (abstain when uncertain); GPT highest hallucination with
  distractors; Gemini generates random words at 500-750 tokens.
- **Accessed:** 2026-04-02

### [27] FinOps Foundation: How Token Pricing Really Works

- **URL:** https://www.finops.org/wg/genai-finops-how-token-pricing-really-works/
- **Type:** Industry working group (FinOps Foundation)
- **Tier:** T2
- **Data extracted:** Output tokens 3-5× more expensive than input. Image ~2×
  text; audio ~8× text. Context window creep: stateless API resends full
  history each turn. Prompt caching: implicit (automatic, free) vs explicit
  (higher upfront, saves on reads). Semantic caching via vector embeddings for
  high-frequency similar queries. Batch processing: 50%+ discount, 24-hour
  delivery. "Cheapest model" paradox: capable models may cost less overall via
  fewer iterations. Hyperscaler pricing varies up to 30% for identical models.
- **Accessed:** 2026-04-02
